name: BA15218 / BA15218F / BA15218N
type: Bipolar dual, low-noise, high slew rate
tagline: ROHM's M5218-class dual (10 MHz, 3 V/µs); Japanese rollers hear cleaner, more extended highs than M5218 or NJM4580.

lineage.note: M5218/M5218A low-noise dual, about 7 MHz GBW per Japanese hobbyist sources; unconfirmed by vendor document.
Reportedly a faster M5218 second source (GBW 7 → 10 MHz). EOL; BA15218F-E2 last-time buy 2026-03-31.

part_numbers.note: DIP8. DigiKey lists it as obsolete.
SIP8; will not fit a DIP8 socket. Likely discontinued, unconfirmed.
SOP8; -E2 tape-and-reel (LCSC C79618). EOL, last-time buy 2026-03-31.

key_specs.value: 4–32 V single; ±3 to ±16 V dual (dual limit unconfirmed)

reputation.summary: A niche Japanese op-amp-rolling favourite rather than a legend. The C-Area wiki heard clean, open, extended highs versus a slightly veiled M5218 and sluggish-bass NJM4580. A note.com headphone-amp test reports firm, low-noise sound. Another hobbyist found it somewhat hard and less spacious. All single-listener impressions.
typical_uses: Op-amp rolling in headphone amps and kits
caveats: EOL: DIP8 BA15218 obsolete, BA15218F-E2 last-time buy 2026-03-31. Remaining supply is old stock.
BA15218N is SIP8 and BA15218F is SOP8; only the plain BA15218 fits a DIP8 socket directly.
Praise comes from a few Japanese hobbyist pages; no measured audio comparisons exist.

counterfeit_notes: No counterfeit reports found. As an EOL part, marketplace lots (e.g. Amazon '5PCS 15218 BA15218 BA15218F BA15218F-T1 BA15218F-E2 SOP8') are of unknown provenance. Buy from authorised distributors while stock lasts.

claims_confirmed: Legacy ROHM sheet covers BA15218/F/N: 4–32 V supply, 1.0 µVrms RIAA, 3 V/µs, 10 MHz, 0.5 mV (https://www.alldatasheet.com/datasheet-pdf/pdf/35931/ROHM/BA15218.html).
ROHM product page shows BA15218F-E2 as EOL / Last Time Buy (https://www.rohm.com/products/amplifiers-and-linear/operational-amplifiers/low-noise/dual-supply-voltage/ba15218f-product).
DigiKey lists the DIP8 BA15218 as obsolete (https://www.digikey.com/product-detail/en/rohm-semiconductor/BA15218/BA15218-ND/658251).
C-Area wiki: clearer, more open highs than M5218 (veiled) and NJM4580 (sluggish bass) (https://w.atwiki.jp/higemouse/pages/104.html).
A note.com headphone-amp BA15218 trial exists (https://note.com/jamjamjamw_w/n/n905ff5d7b92c).
Japanese hobbyists reportedly call it ROHM's faster M5218 second source (GBW 7 → 10 MHz); exact page not pinned (https://w.atwiki.jp/higemouse/pages/104.html).
